Nov 18, 2026

Automatically retrieve SAML IdP signing certificates

Cloudflare OneAccess

Cloudflare Access can retrieve signing certificates from a SAML identity provider's metadata endpoint. Your IdP can publish replacement certificates without requiring you to upload each one to Access.

In your generic SAML identity provider configuration, set Signing certificate source to Fetch certificates from IdP metadata and enter the IdP metadata URL. The endpoint must return SAML metadata XML over public HTTPS, without authentication or redirects. It must not return a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS).

For API configurations, use metadata_url instead of manual certificate fields:

Access caches the certificates and does not poll the endpoint.

Removing a compromised certificate from metadata does not immediately revoke the cached certificate or existing Access sessions. For setup, planned rotation, and emergency replacement guidance, refer to Discover IdP signing certificates.

Nov 17, 2026

Configure a separate WAN gateway for each appliance in a high availability site

Cloudflare One ApplianceCloudflare OneCloudflare WAN

You can now give each Cloudflare One Appliance in a high availability (HA) site its own default gateway on a static WAN. Before this change, both appliances in an HA pair shared the same WAN gateway. Now each appliance can connect to its own Internet circuit, such as a different ISP for each appliance, with its own static IP and gateway.

  • In the dashboard, when you configure a static WAN on an HA site, enter the secondary appliance's gateway in the new Secondary gateway address field, next to Primary gateway address.
  • In the API, set static_addressing.secondary_gateway_address when you create or update a WAN. To remove the value with a PATCH request, set it to null.

The field is optional. If you leave it blank, the secondary appliance uses the primary gateway address, which matches how HA sites worked before. You can only use this field on sites in HA mode.

For details, refer to About high availability configurations.

Nov 17, 2026

Investigate user risk events in a timeline

Risk Score

User Risk Scoring now groups risk behavior instances in a timeline. Each group highlights its trigger and shows later detections in time order.

Customize the date range to focus on the events you want to investigate. Select a timeline marker to view its events. The sequence helps security teams follow how risk events relate during investigations.

Switch to Table to return to the existing table view whenever you prefer.

User Risk Scoring is available on Enterprise plans.

For more information, refer to User risk score.

Nov 16, 2026

Cloudflare One adds Periodic Beaconing Traffic detection

Cloudflare OneGateway

Cloudflare One now includes Periodic Beaconing Traffic as a risk behavior. It analyzes Gateway HTTP traffic for regular check-ins to the same destination.

Cloudflare flags a user after more than 30 contacts to the same destination in six hours. Contacts must be evenly spaced, from 10 seconds to about 12 minutes apart. Few other users in your organization contact that destination.

Detection uses traffic behavior only. It does not use threat intelligence, categories, or reputation. Malware can check in with a command-and-control (C2) server this way, but legitimate software also checks in regularly. Treat each event as a lead to investigate, not proof that a destination is C2.

By default, the behavior is off and its risk level is Info. To turn it on, go to Risk score > Risk behaviors. Cloudflare reports a continuing beacon once. Events usually arrive 3 to 6 hours after the six-hour window closes.

Periodic Beaconing Traffic is available on Enterprise plans.

Nov 12, 2026

Cloudflare Tunnel extends URL normalization

Cloudflare TunnelCloudflare Tunnel for SASE

Starting from version 2026.11.0, Cloudflare Tunnel extends the URL normalization introduced in 2026.10.0. Normalization now handles semicolon-delimited path parameters before matching ingress rules. This improves security for tunnels with rules that require Cloudflare Access validation. The URL path sent to your origin stays the same.

Starting 2027-02-08, new cloudflared releases will turn on URL normalization by default. This replaces the previously announced date of 2027-01-25, giving you time to test the updated behavior. Upgrade to version 2026.11.0 or later and test your path-based routing before that date, including rules that match paths containing semicolons. Configurations without rules requiring Access validation are unaffected.

This setting is currently off by default. To turn it on, run:

Alternatively, set TUNNEL_DISABLE_PATH_NORMALIZATION=false on each cloudflared replica and restart it.

For more information, refer to ingress matching and Access validation at the origin.

Nov 11, 2026

GitHub automatically detects leaked Access service tokens

AccessCloudflare One

GitHub secret scanning automatically detects Cloudflare Access service token secrets exposed in public repositories and reports them to Cloudflare. Access then disables the affected token and emails account administrators.

Other secret scanning tools can identify Access service tokens using their consistent Client Secret format: cfast_, followed by 40 alphanumeric characters and an eight-character hexadecimal checksum. For tools that support custom detection rules, use this regular expression to find possible secrets:

This pattern applies to Client Secrets created on or after August 26, 2026, not legacy 64-character hexadecimal secrets. Matching the pattern does not validate the checksum or confirm that the secret is active. For details, refer to Client Secret format.

Recover a leaked service token

Before you can re-enable a leaked token, you must rotate its secret.

Leaked secrets do not support a rotation grace period. When you rotate one, the previous secret is discarded immediately. Update your services with the new secret, then re-enable the token.

For API rotations, omit previous_client_secret_expires_at. A future expiration returns 400. Attempting to re-enable the token before rotation returns 409.

For recovery steps and leak metadata fields, refer to Recover a leaked service token.

Nov 10, 2026

Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.9.2663.1)

Cloudflare One Client

A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the beta releases downloads page.

This release includes the following highlights:

  • Added automatic endpoint selection for Global Acceleration. When Global Acceleration is enabled for an organization, the client connects to the Global Acceleration endpoints while the device is in the acceleration region and to the standard anycast endpoints otherwise, and reconnects when a network change moves the device between them without requiring action from the user. The Connectivity page shows which tunnel and API endpoints are in use, and users who are allowed to override the selection can choose endpoints in Settings.
  • Added protection against unauthorized modification or uninstallation of the Cloudflare One Client. When enabled, the user will be asked to provide an administrator-generated code when trying to uninstall the client, which will otherwise be blocked. Users, including administrators, also can no longer stop the client service, and attempts to authorize an uninstall with a code or token, whether accepted or rejected, are reported to Cloudflare.
  • Added a Diagnostics page to the client that shows the connection status and health, live tunnel and device metrics, network details and the results of DEX tests in one place. Users can run a speed test from the page that compares performance inside and outside the tunnel while the client is connected. The Troubleshooting tools button collects a full warp-diag bundle, or runs a captive portal test that briefly reconnects Wi-Fi, and saves the result to the Desktop, so users no longer need to run warp-diag from a terminal.
  • The client now shows a banner when the network limits the tunnel MTU to a degraded or critically low value. The banner clears when the MTU recovers or the client disconnects.

Additional changes and improvements

  • The client now applies tunnel MTUs between 1147 and 1199 bytes measured by Path MTU Discovery. Previously the client ignored these values and kept a larger MTU, which could drop larger packets on networks such as mobile hotspots while the client showed as connected.
  • When Path MTU Discovery is enabled, the client now accepts larger packets from Cloudflare instead of limiting them to the size it uses for its own outbound packets.
  • When Path MTU Discovery measures an IPv6 path MTU below 1280 bytes, the client now reconnects over IPv4 and keeps preferring IPv4 until the network changes. Previously the client could stay on a smaller tunnel MTU over IPv6 on networks where IPv4 supports larger packets.
  • Access reauthentication requests now trust certificates in the operating system's certificate store, so reauthentication works on networks that perform TLS inspection.
  • For Zero Trust deployments, the client now records a traceroute of the network path outside the tunnel when the tunnel degrades or fails to connect. warp-diag includes the same trace.
  • warp-diag now includes redacted copies of the deployed MDM files and the names, but not the values, of stored registration secrets. It reports a QUIC path MTU only when one was measured.
  • Added the MDM parameters mdm_file_debounce_secs (1–60) and mdm_file_unavailable_debounce_secs (0–300), which set how long the client waits before applying a changed MDM file and before acting on a missing or unreadable one.
  • Added the MDM parameters managed_network_probe_interval_secs (30–300, default 30) and managed_network_probe_count (0 disables probing, 1–10, or -1 to keep probing until a managed network is found; default 1). After a registration or network change finds no managed network, the client now rechecks, so a device doesn't stay on the default profile because of a transient connection failure. Set the count to 0 to keep the previous behavior.
  • Added the multicast network policy and MDM setting (allow or drop, default drop). When set to allow, the client sends traffic for multicast addresses through the tunnel instead of dropping it, for networks that use multicast ranges for other traffic.
  • In proxy mode for Zero Trust, the client now sends hostnames from HTTP/HTTPS and SOCKS5 requests to Cloudflare for resolution instead of resolving them on the device.
  • The Connectivity page now shows the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses assigned to the tunnel while the client is connected.
  • When the app cannot reach the client service, the home screen now says why (service not running, not accepting connections, not responding, or connection dropped and reconnecting). It shows an error code and a Learn more link instead of "IPC error".
  • The client now shows a notification when an administrator removes the user's selected virtual network, and shows a specific message when the user selects a virtual network that is no longer available.
  • The consumer client home screen now shows when the connection is post-quantum encrypted.
  • warp-cli target list now accepts --hostname to filter targets by one or more comma-separated hostnames.
  • DEX HTTP tests now send a default User-Agent that identifies the Cloudflare One Client when the test does not configure one.
  • Reduced CPU usage by the Windows Capability Access Manager service (camsvc) caused by the client's Wi-Fi queries.
  • Reduced the client UI's memory usage.
  • The client UI no longer starts WMIC or PowerShell processes to collect memory information for crash reports.
  • Fixed installs failing with error 1603 on devices with Windows App Control (WDAC) policies, because some files inside the installer's custom actions were not signed. All components of the installer are now signed.
  • Fixed the installer asking the user to close running applications during an upgrade, downgrade or uninstall because other programs loaded the client's Visual C++ runtime libraries through the system PATH. The client now loads these libraries from a private folder so that closing other applications is unnecessary.
  • Fixed reinstalling the same version of the client from its MSI removing the updater service, which stopped the client from updating.
  • Fixed the client window appearing blank or white after an upgrade, at sign-in, after waking from sleep, or after a display change.
  • Fixed the client UI freezing and no longer showing status updates after the device woke from sleep.
  • Fixed the client UI looking for one of its libraries in a directory that standard users can create before looking in the installation directory.
  • Fixed a local user being able to crash the client service by sending a crafted query to the local DNS resolver.
  • Fixed the client service restarting when a firewall update for captive portal detection stalled while the device was asleep.
  • Fixed the client service leaking handles to processes after they exited, which could leave those processes listed as running.
  • Fixed the client getting stuck in a disconnected state on Windows on Arm devices because leftover tunnel adapters were not removed.
  • Fixed Windows resetting the Wi-Fi adapter after sign-in or a Wi-Fi restart when the client's firewall rules in Exclude split tunnel mode blocked Windows network connectivity checks. The client now allows those checks.
  • Fixed the client missing some network configuration changes after the first change was detected.
  • Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade that switched between consumer and Zero Trust registrations. The client now clears the mismatched registration so the user can register again.
  • Fixed the client continuing to use the previous tunnel protocol after a key rotation for a protocol change failed. The client now retries the rotation the next time it connects.
  • Fixed service token enrollment failing when it ran shortly after the service token was created. The client now retries while the new token becomes available.
  • Fixed the client reconnecting repeatedly when Global Acceleration automatic endpoint selection was enabled on devices in the acceleration region, and fixed the client keeping its previous data center after the selected endpoints changed.
  • Fixed a hostname-based split tunnel entry not taking effect until the next reconnect after its firewall rule failed to apply.
  • Fixed the client service failing to start when a split tunnel address in mdm.xml had no prefix length. A bare IP address is now treated as a single host.
  • Fixed a single malformed element in mdm.xml causing the client to ignore the whole file. warp-diag now includes the file as written.
  • Fixed warp-cli dns fallback add accepting an empty domain, which sent all DNS queries to the local resolver instead of Gateway. Fallback domain and split tunnel entries are now normalized, so removing an entry matches regardless of case or a trailing dot.
  • Fixed the DNS proxy caching answers for longer than the TTL of a CNAME record in the chain.
  • Fixed warp-cli registration license reporting an error on slow networks even though the license was applied, which left the client registered to a WARP+ account it did not recognize.
  • Fixed warp-cli debug network showing an all-zero interface GUID.
  • Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) results being reported with timestamps offset from the actual time after the system clock was corrected.

Known issues

  • A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While our client includes a mitigation for this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.
  • After an administrator removes a virtual network from a device profile or changes its default network, the virtual network list in the client may continue to show the previous networks until the client is restarted. This is a display issue only: the device connects to the networks its profile allows, and selecting a removed network is rejected without changing the connection. The warp-cli vnet command shows the current list. This will be addressed prior to the next GA release.

Email securityCloudflare One

Email security now has a unified search bar for investigations. It replaces the Email Screener side modal and makes searches easier to refine.

Search with keywords or field:value filters. Autocomplete suggests filters and values as you type. Add terms and press Enter to refine results, or select From, To, Disposition, Status, or Threat type values in results. Narrow results with a date preset or custom range.

Nov 6, 2026

Sign in to Cloudflare Access with passkeys

AccessCloudflare One

Cloudflare Access supports passkeys as a login method for protected applications and the App Launcher. Users can sign in with a passkey saved on their device, security key, or password manager instead of entering a one-time PIN or configuring an identity provider.

Users verify their identity with an existing login method once before enrolling a passkey. Administrators choose which applications accept passkeys and can remove a user's registered passkeys. Access policies still determine whether a user can access an application.

For setup and enrollment instructions, refer to Passkeys.

Nov 6, 2026

Cloudflare One adds fast flux detection to UEBA

Cloudflare One

Cloudflare One now includes fast flux detection as a predefined risk behavior for user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA). When enabled, detections contribute to a user's risk score.

Fast flux is a DNS technique that rapidly changes the IP addresses returned for a domain. Threat actors can use it to make malicious infrastructure harder to track and take down. Detecting it can help security teams identify potentially risky activity and investigate it sooner.

To turn on fast flux detection, go to Risk score > Risk behaviors in the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard.

Fast flux detection is available on Enterprise plans.

For more information, refer to User risk score.

Nov 5, 2026

Set expiration dates for Email security policies

Email security

Email security now lets you set an expiration date when creating an allow or block policy. This helps you apply temporary policy changes without removing them manually.

After the selected date passes, the policy expires and no longer applies.

This feature is available to all Email security customers, regardless of plan.

Nov 4, 2026

Block data entry with Browser Isolation without losing search, copy, and zoom (beta)

Browser IsolationCloudflare One

Isolation policies now support a third keyboard option in beta: Allow read-only actions. Previously, the keyboard setting was binary — allow all input or block everything. With Allow read-only actions, you can block data entry while preserving the built-in browser actions your users depend on.

In Allow read-only actions mode, users can still find in page, select all, copy, print, and zoom. All other keyboard input is blocked from reaching the isolated page. Copy and print remain subject to their own policy settings, so the controls compose instead of overriding each other. For example, setting the keyboard to Allow read-only actions and copy to Do not allow lets users search and zoom but prevents them from copying content.

To use this feature, set Keyboard to Allow read-only actions in your isolation policy settings. Via the API, set keyboard to enable_read_only_actions in the biso_admin_controls object with version set to v2.

For more information, refer to Keyboard.

Nov 4, 2026

New managed rule to help mitigate CVE-2026-98432.

Cloudflare Network Firewall

Cloudflare Network Firewall has a new managed rule to help mitigate the Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎):

  • Rule name: Block CVE-2026-98432 ↗︎ traffic
  • Rule ID: 6a4df2bf984946a88c74b07349557e83

The rule is disabled by default. To use it:

  1. Go to Networking > Firewall Policies > Managed Rulesets.
  2. Enable the rule with action Log first.
  3. Review traffic that matches the rule.
  4. If the matching traffic is not expected for your environment, change the action to Block.

For more information on enabling managed rulesets, refer to Enable managed rulesets.

For more details about the vulnerability, including an agent assessment prompt and evidence sources, refer to the Cloudflare Radar Zero Wire briefing ↗︎.

Nov 4, 2026

Steer Cloudflare One users and private networks to the same endpoint with session affinity and hash steering in private load balancers

Load BalancingCloudflare TunnelCloudflare Mesh

Private load balancers can now keep each user on the same endpoint. This helps with applications that keep session state on a single server.

Two options are available:

  • Hash endpoint steering. In the dashboard, set a pool's Endpoint steering to Hash. Each user is mapped to an endpoint within the pool.
  • Session affinity. With the API, set session_affinity to ip_cookie on the load balancer. Each user stays on the same endpoint while it remains healthy and your pools do not change. Refer to Session affinity.

For traffic from the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare identifies the user by their device, so a user stays on the same endpoint even if their IP address changes. For other traffic, such as from a Cloudflare WAN site, Cloudflare uses the source IP address.

This works for endpoints reached through Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Mesh, and Cloudflare WAN. Affinity pins the endpoint, not the cloudflared or Mesh replica that carries the traffic.

To learn how private load balancing fits with your connectors, refer to Load balance private network traffic.

Oct 30, 2026

Inspect provisioned users and groups with the SCIM population viewer

Cloudflare OneAccess

The SCIM population viewer lets you inspect the users and groups provisioned to Cloudflare One by each identity provider. You can check which resources Cloudflare has received without making API requests or opening a support ticket.

In Zero Trust > Integrations > Identity providers, select a user or group count in SCIM resources to open the viewer. You can:

  • Search users by username, email, name, or resource ID, and groups by name or resource ID.
  • Inspect resource attributes in formatted or JSON views.
  • View group members and compare Cloudflare and IdP resource IDs with provisioning logs.
  • Delete individual resources from the Cloudflare SCIM population when you have edit permission.

The viewer shows provisioned resources rather than provisioning event history. Use SCIM provisioning logs to investigate failed requests. Existing SCIM deprovisioning and policy behavior remain unchanged.

For dashboard instructions and API examples, refer to View SCIM users and groups.

Oct 30, 2026

Cloudflare WAN supports regional Gateway HTTP inspection

Data Localization SuiteCloudflare WANCloudflare One

Cloudflare WAN traffic can now use a Gateway processing region with Regional Services. HTTPS traffic enters a Cloudflare data center (that may be outside the selected region) via an IPsec or GRE tunnel, or through Direct CNI, and remains encrypted until Gateway forwards it to the selected region for TLS decryption and HTTP inspection. This feature gives organizations control over where their sensitive traffic is processed, supporting their data sovereignty goals.

This feature requires unified routing. The processing region applies to Gateway HTTP traffic and does not apply to Gateway DNS or network policy processing.

Contact your account team to configure a processing region. For supported regions, configuration details, and limitations, refer to Data residency for Cloudflare One.
